Where things stand
Your site today
bignosefullbody.com

The current site on Squarespace. Good bones: the photo, the stamp, the hours. The shop underneath is a long tagged list.

What we noticed

  • The catalogue is the asset. Six hundred bottles, every one tagged by grape, region, organic, biodynamic, kosher, unoaked. That tagging is real work and it should carry over intact.
  • The shop is hard to browse. "Shop" leads to a page explaining how to search. Reserve-list bottles and everyday bottles sit in the same long lists with no photos.
  • The offers are buried. Free Park Slope delivery, daily tastings at 15% off, HALF5 and CASE15 discounts. These are the reasons to buy from you and not from an app.
  • You're paying a platform to be a platform. A subscription, a card rate, and possibly a cut of every online sale. Whatever the figure, some of it is buying tiers you don't use.

The platform
What runs it
codanomix

A website system we build, host and look after ourselves.

codanomix is our own platform for small businesses that sell real things: shops, restaurants, galleries, places to stay. One login runs the whole site, the shop, the stock and the orders.

Where it comes from

The 2026 rebuild of a content platform our studio has run for client sites for more than a decade. Same team, same code we answer for, rewritten for how the web works now.

What makes it different

It isn't a template marketplace. Each site is a separate, private install with its own database and its own files, on servers we run. Nothing is shared with another customer, and no third party gets your sales data.

Who you deal with

Support is by online ticket, answered from London by the team that built the platform. It's the same people for the site, the shop and the hosting, so nothing gets passed to a third party.

Under the hood
Hosting, security and the boring parts done properly

Modern, private, and built to be left alone

Hosting

  • Amazon Web Services, with Cloudflare's network in front so pages are served from the edge nearest the customer.
  • Published pages are plain, static files. Nothing to slow down, nothing to fall over on a Saturday night.
  • Your site is its own private install: own database, own files, own system account. Nothing shared.
  • Daily backups. Updates and security patches applied by us, not left for you to click.

Security

  • HTTPS everywhere with strict transport security; TLS 1.2 and up at the edge, with post-quantum key exchange already on.
  • A strict Content Security Policy with no inline scripts, so injected code cannot run in your admin.
  • Passkey sign-in, bcrypt-hashed passwords, login throttling, forgery-proof forms, hardened sessions.
  • Card details never touch our servers: payment is handled by Stripe. Order links are single-use and rotate.
  • If we ever need to sign in to help you, it's through a signed, one-time, sixty-second door that leaves an audit line on both sides.

Spec

  • codanomix version 1.0.1839, released 3 September 2026. Runs on PHP 8.5 and MariaDB on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS.
  • Shop pages carry Product structured data, canonical URLs and a sitemap, so Google lists bottles with prices and availability.
  • Stripe for cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay. Other processors available.
  • Email sent through Amazon SES from your own domain, with DKIM and DMARC.
  • Works on phones, tablets and the shop's laptop. No app to install.

What happens next

  • We listen first. This meeting is about what the site needs to do for the shop, not about numbers.
  • Then a written proposal. After we've talked, we'll put a proposal together that covers the build, the hosting and support, and the move from Squarespace.
  • Your figures are yours. If you're comfortable sharing what the current site costs, we'll make the proposal a straight comparison. If not, we'll still make it a fair one.
  • You own everything either way. The domain, the design, the catalogue, the customer list. If you ever leave, it comes with you.
